Title: Tiny Harlots
Source Situation / Theme: Babysitting leads Tara to piano, dance, voice, and theater; performance widens her world while modesty rules produce shame and contradiction.
Design Extraction: Performance creates visibility, skill, and alternative identity, but being seen can also feel dangerous.
Game Transformation: Build a performance system around rhythm, listening, movement, costume choice, ensemble trust, and public confidence.
Act: Act II - Cracks in the Story
Guardrail: Do not sexualize a teen character or make modesty conflict into a joke.

Title: Perfect in His Generations
Source Situation / Theme: Tara performs in Annie while the household prepares for Y2K and the end of the world; the failed prediction leaves her father diminished.
Design Extraction: Two countdowns can occupy the same life: a creative future and an expected catastrophe.
Game Transformation: Run parallel preparation clocks for a performance and a household emergency plan, forcing resource and relationship choices.
Act: Act II - Cracks in the Story
Guardrail: Represent belief with complexity; do not use apocalypse expectations as simple comedy.

Title: Shield of Feathers
Source Situation / Theme: After Y2K, another Arizona trip briefly lifts the father's mood, while conflict over a grandmother's cancer treatment returns.
Design Extraction: Sunlight and travel may change mood without resolving a worldview conflict; care can become a loyalty test.
Game Transformation: Use a desert travel chapter with caregiving tasks, family arguments, and two medical systems that have different strengths and limits.
Act: Act II - Cracks in the Story
Guardrail: Never present serious illness as proof that one character deserves suffering.

Title: Instinct
Source Situation / Theme: Shawn helps Tara tame a wild horse and becomes protective, but warmth shifts toward aggression when others are present.
Design Extraction: A relationship can offer real skill and rescue while also carrying warning signs.
Game Transformation: Create a horse-training partnership where trust grows through action and the player learns to read changing body language.
Act: Act II - Cracks in the Story
Guardrail: Do not convert coercive control into a romance reward loop.

Title: Fish Eyes
Source Situation / Theme: A trucking trip creates closeness with Shawn through jokes and shared work, while his treatment of Sadie exposes control and cruelty.
Design Extraction: Travel creates private intimacy, but how someone treats a third person may reveal more than how they treat the player.
Game Transformation: Use a long-haul mission with vehicle care, wordplay dialogue, roadside tasks, and a witness-based boundary decision.
Act: Act II - Cracks in the Story
Guardrail: Make the third character an independent agent, not merely evidence about Silas.

Title: Silence in the Churches
Source Situation / Theme: National crisis is absorbed into an apocalyptic family story; Tara faces puberty, shame, violence, and a community that does not name what is happening.
Design Extraction: Public events are interpreted through local worldviews, while silence can protect belonging and preserve harm.
Game Transformation: Let radio news, a meetinghouse service, and a private threat produce competing interpretations and a choice about whom to tell.
Act: Act II - Cracks in the Story
Guardrail: Avoid reenacting 9/11 as spectacle; use fictional national news and focus on interpretation.

Title: My Feet No Longer Touch Earth
Source Situation / Theme: New technology and ACT study open possibility while dangerous construction work and Shawn's head injury pull Tara back into care.
Design Extraction: Growth occurs beside crisis. Learning time, paid work, and caregiving compete for the same hours.
Game Transformation: Combine an early-internet research puzzle, test preparation, and a construction rescue with persistent schedule consequences.
Act: Act II - Cracks in the Story
Guardrail: Medical consequences remain serious and non-repeatable.

Title: No More a Child
Source Situation / Theme: Tara realizes her future cannot contain both her desires and her father's total authority; her mother unexpectedly urges her to continue.
Design Extraction: Independence begins as a private decision before it becomes visible departure.
Game Transformation: Create a hidden study plan, work schedule, and private alliance with Ruth that the player can protect, reveal, or abandon.
Act: Act II - Cracks in the Story
Guardrail: Do not imply that one courageous speech instantly defeats structural control.
